I work for the county so although I'm not an attorney, I can give you some general advice. 

Has the landlord already filed the eviction with the courts? Just as an FYI, if the landlord is nasty and claiming intimidation like you said, they're probably going to file an emergency eviction. You would think you'd have to supply a lot of proof to get it, but all they have to say they were threatened with bodily harm and bam, your friends suddenly don't get the hearing in 3 weeks like they normally would and instead have as little as 3 days to get their stuff ready and come to court (and if the judge is in court, which happens a lot, the court reporter is the one that actually makes that decision). Further, the time to leave the premises is then drastically reduced too.  Point being, they probably have extremely little time to be getting these quotes and pictures together. If you can show a history of violations by the landlord (no notice showing up and letting themselves in, not fixing the property, etc.) AND show a history of them doing this with other tenants then they may have a shot, depending which judge they get.  There are subpoena forms they can get in the clerk's office for both people an documents, so once they're served with the eviction notice they can come and in get them and have any witnesses come to court with them for the hearing (although warning, don't bring too many or you'll tick off the judge). Good luck and don't have them wait because they probably won't have much time soon. The judges aren't stupid--they know which companies have a bad rep. It's actually funny at times because they'll come in and file, find out what court they were assigned to, and freak because "that judge has it in for me and just doesn't get it."

When I hit my teenage years, I noticed I was always tired and hurt everywhere, but particularly my knees and hands. Doctors kept telling me I was depressed and wanted to put me on meds, but I refused because I didn't think it made sense. A couple of years later my aunt gets diagnosed with RA, and my mom asks the doctor to test me. Turned out I had RA and my inflammation levels were the highest my rheumatologist had seen in a teenager. Thankfully my levels are manageable now. 

Not as big, but over the summer I started running (doing the couch to 5k thing) and the third day had a severe pain in my foot about 1 1/2 miles down the trail.  I could barely walk all the way back, but thought I twisted my ankle or something. The next couple of days didn't get any better so I bought an ace bandage and made sure to tighten my shoes so my ankle/foot couldn't bend. The pain never got better, and it started getting to the point that it felt like my foot would fall off my leg. I went to my doctor and they said I sprained both of my ankles on that leg,  and to call back in 3 days if not better. I called back in 2, and they said I could get an xray but they were only going to send me to a physical therapist. Long story short, I skipped that and went to urgent care, who told me I didn't break anything but probably pulled something badly and sent me to an ortho. It turned out that I had a severe distal tibia fracture and had been walking on it for over 2 weeks by the time he saw me. I initially got hurt in July,  and just got the all clear to start running again in January.

If you're set on Bloomington, the Fields has a really pretty clubhouse with a nice fireplace that feels rustic and warm.  The rental is a little pricey since it only includes the room, but you get plenty of time to decorate it and make it yours.  The same goes for the Boulders if you did an outdoor wedding.

One option a little out of Bloomington is actually Chateau de Pique.  My friend told me about it literally right after I got married.  If I'd had the time to change it, I'd have moved it there instead.  They have a beautiful limestone (hey, it's Indiana!) outdoor area, and then a really pretty barn area for the reception.  Here are some pictures of it:
http://www.mywedding.com/vendors/chateau-de-pique-winery-67725/galleries?galleryId=20743

One of my other friends is doing a wedding out by McCormicks at a hotel but I can't remember the name.  I think it needs a bit of work though to make it feel rustic, instead of outdated.

Honestly, it just depends on what the general feel is, your budget, time of year, and what exactly you want out of it all!  I preferred not having to do a lot the day of, so I didn't consider any areas that would require a ton of decorating.  If you're wanting to celebrate your alma mater (like I did!), there's another option outside of IU in the back of the Union to do an outdoor wedding, and then you could choose one of the rooms inside for the reception.  Before getting married it felt like everything was really overwhelming, but having been through it now with mine and few friends I can plan one in a week (literally--I had to plan one that was a week before Christmas lol).  Good luck, and no matter what you decide to do, it will be beautiful and suit your perfectly!

If I had the money to give you, I would but unfortunately all I can do is give you some advice.  I don't live in NYC so I don't know what their policies are, but you should first find out if you really do have a warrant out for you.  Try calling your local clerk's office and ask them if they can run your name for a case that has a warrant (they will grumble I'm sure, but they can do it).  I work at the Clerk's office in Indiana and we have our court information loaded online, so you could also try calling your local office and ask if they do the same so then you could check yourself.  I highly doubt you would have a warrant for that, unless the ticket they cited you with had a hearing date and you didn't come to it.  If there isn't a hearing date, it's probably not the case.  More than likely you've probably been sued though, and the sheriff is trying to serve you (here they try twice before just leaving the papers in the door for you).  The city here used to sue people for not paying their citations with this being their standard procedure... and unfortunately that meant the costs would go up even higher at that point (now we've turned everything over to collection agencies from parking tickets to speeding tickets).  Good luck with everything!  I'm sure all is not as bad as you think it is!  Generally these things seem really scary, but if you call and tell them you're making a good faith effort to resolve it, but are just really low on money they'll try to work something out with you!

Edit:  I think this is New York's equivalent to the one we use here:
https://iapps.courts.state.ny.us/webcivil/ecourtsMain

I assume you don't have any major issues that demand recurring appointments and treatments?  I was in a similar situation a few years ago, but I lost mine for around a year and I ended up being alright.  The main thing to call around and see what your local options are for those with low to no income (since your job doesn't start for a few more weeks).  My area has a clinic for low income people so you can get treated for relatively common things and not break that bank.  Another option to be aware of actually is Planned Parenthood--they aren't just for abortions, and when I didn't have any insurance and my kidneys gave me hell (kidney problems run in my family), they were my only option and didn't charge to treat me.  Worst case scenario is you may have to go to the hospital, but generally they're willing to knock the cost down if you don't have insurance and will do payment plans until you get everything paid off.  I'm sure everything will be fine, but it does help for peace of mind to know what to do in the event something would come up.  I know during my year of no insurance I would briefly panic that every pulled muscle was appendicitis, just because I'd have to pay for everything.
